newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen up on carryover, peso firm.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen up on carryover, peso firm.

text.p: Dealers saw stocks extending their record march at the open on Tuesday in a continuation of Monday's trend, although they did not rule out intraday profit-taking stemming from an unsteady Dow Jones.
"We ought to see profit-taking, but we have plenty og buy orders left from yesterday," a desk trader said.
Technical analysts placed resistance at 5,170 points on the IPC index, up from Monday's record close of 5,135.24.
Traders expected the peso to open firm on capital inflow into financial markets and because of peso demand to bid in the central bank primary auction.

Banks could exercise dollar put options during the session and thus cap peso firmness, they added. Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.8025/8125 per dollar for the 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.8050/8100 per dollar, compared to Monday's close of 7.8120/7.8150.
Overnight rates on Cetes were seen opening slightly up from a late dip to 19.25 percent during Monday, but with upside pressure limited by ample market liquidity.
